title: Enterprise onboarding — support process, integration, escalation, known issues & QBR playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents the end-to-end enterprise onboarding and ongoing support process for Redwood Inference customers. It unifies integration guidance, escalation procedures, known issues and workarounds, and the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) / health-check cadence so Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE teams operate from a single, actionable source.

Scope: Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private deployments) during the onboarding period (weeks 0-12) and for steady-state accounts where QBRs and escalations occur.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-deployment to under 21 days for standard integrations.
- Resolve P0 incidents according to SLA (2-hour incident response, 8-hour remediation plan).
- Ensure customers receive a clear handoff to Support + SRE with documented runbooks and playbook artifacts.

Key contacts and ownership
- Customer Success (Primary owner): weekly cadence, QBRs, adoption metrics.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): integration design, onboarding runbooks, validation tests.
- Support (Tier 1/2): first-line troubleshooting and ticketing.
- Eng SRE / Serving Runtime: Tier 3 for production incidents and performance regression.
- Product: roadmap alignment items captured during QBR and escalations.

Pre-onboarding checklist (to be completed before week 0)
1. Contract and account provisioning confirmed (billing, tenant ID, legal).
2. Customer access matrix (API keys, VPC peering or VPN details, KMS/HSM info).
3. Security & compliance checklist signed (data residency, retention, PII handling).
4. Kickoff meeting scheduled with stakeholders: CS, SE, customer engineering, security.
5. Baseline workload profile supplied: expected qps, typical prompt lengths, peak hours, 99th percentile latency goals.

Integration guide (high-level steps)
- Phase 1: Design & network setup
  - Validate network connectivity: outbound IP allowlist or VPC peering checklist.
  - Confirm TLS and mTLS requirements and KMS integration steps.
  - Confirm model & endpoint selection (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private).
- Phase 2: Implementation & validation
  - Provide SDK quickstart and sample prompts.
  - Run smoke tests: simple text generation, streaming test, embedding sanity checks.
  - Run load tests (recommended): 5k short prompt tokens at expected qps; measure tail latency and token cost.
- Phase 3: Production cutover
  - Schedule cutover window and rollback plan.
  - Validate observability: per-route latency, token usage, and error rates visible in Redwood Console.

Integration configuration table (recommended minimums)
| Area | Recommended config | Owner |
|------|--------------------|-------|
| Auth | API keys + rotating service principal | Customer + CS |
| Network | VPC peering or static IP allowlist; 1-hour connection test | SE |
| Monitoring | Route-level dashboards, token-level cost metrics, tracing enabled | CS + Eng Platform |
| Performance | Expected SLOs: P95 latency < 300ms for short prompts; throughput target documented | Customer + SRE |

Support process and SLAs
- Ticketing: All inbound issues must be logged in Zendesk (or configured enterprise ticketing) with customer ID, environment, and severity assigned.
- Severity definitions:
  - P0 (Critical): Production outage or data loss; system unusable. Response: 2-hour acknowledgement, 8-hour remediation plan, continuous incident bridge.
  - P1 (High): Severe degradation impacting many users. Response: 4-hour acknowledgement, 24-hour remediation plan.
  - P2 (Medium): Functional degradation affecting a subset of users. Response: 24-hour acknowledgement, regular updates.
  - P3 (Low): Minor issue or feature request. Response: standard SLA during business hours.
- Escalation matrix (contact sequence): Support L1 -> Support L2 -> SE on-call -> Eng SRE on-call -> Product/VPs if SLA thresholds missed. Maintain contact roster in PagerDuty.

Escalation playbook (step-by-step)
1. Triage (Support L1)
  - Collect: customer tenant ID, API request/response samples, timestamps, full request headers, model and version, route name.
  - Run quick checks: account quota, recent deploys, config changes, token usage spikes.
2. Containment (Support L2 / SE)
  - If client-side: provide immediate mitigation steps (rate-limiting guidance, retry/backoff examples, reduce prompt size, enable caching).
  - If server-side: gather logs, start incident bridge, reproduce issue in staging if available.
3. Root cause & remediation (SE + SRE)
  - Execute targeted diagnostics: kernel perf traces, KV cache hit rates, GPU utilization, model version diffs.
  - Apply temporary mitigations: route to fallback model variant, increase capacity on Dedicated pool, enable cache warmup.
4. Post-incident follow-up
  - Document RCA in incident tracker within 72 hours.
  - Create runbook updates if the issue shows a repeatable pattern.
  - Notify customer with remediation summary and timeline for permanent fix.

Known issues & workarounds (selected entries)
- Issue: Elevated token cost after model upgrade
  - Symptom: Token consumption increases ~20% after new model version deployed.
  - Workaround: Use quantization profile recommended in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles, enforce max_tokens and stop sequences at client side. Revert to previous model if regression persists.
- Issue: Increased tail latency on long-context prompts
  - Symptom: P99 spikes for prompts > 1024 tokens.
  - Workaround: Use chunked prompt strategy (split context into embeddings + retrieval), increase KV cache size on Dedicated pools, or use a model variant optimized for long context.
- Issue: Intermittent 5xx errors for streaming endpoints
  - Symptom: Streaming connection resets after ~30s under medium load.
  - Workaround: Verify network MTU and keepalive settings, enable client reconnect with idempotency tokens, configure connection retry with exponential backoff.

Support runbooks & operational checks (examples)
- Daily checks (Support L1): account health dashboard, error rate >0.5% alerts, token quota spikes, active incidents list.
- Weekly checks (CS + SE): integration smoke test, billing usage review, pending support tickets >7 days.
- Monthly checks (SRE): capacity headroom report (GPU pool utilization < 70% target), regression alert review, model quality drift metrics.

Health checks & QBR template (30/60/90 and ongoing)
- Health check cadence:
  - Week 1: onboarding health call — confirm network/auth, run smoke tests, baseline metrics.
  - Week 4: performance review — latency, error rates, cost per token, initial adoption metrics.
  - Week 12: production readiness signoff — SLA acceptance, runbooks delivered, operational contacts confirmed.
  - Quarterly: full QBR covering adoption, ROI, roadmap items, and model/serving recommendations.
- QBR agenda (recommended)
  1. Executive summary: adoption highlights and top metrics.
  2. Reliability review: incidents, RCA status, SLO attainment.
  3. Cost & usage: token spend, embedding usage, opportunities for quantization/batching.
  4. Product & roadmap alignment: requested features and planned releases.
  5. Action items & owners: 90-day plan with owners.

Operational metrics and dashboards to include
- Per-route request rate and error rate (1m/5m/1h aggregations).
- Token-level spend by route and by model.
- Latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) per model and per deployment.
- Cache hit ratio and batching efficiency metrics.

Handoff and closure checklist (post-onboarding)
- All runbooks and incident playbooks added to customer folder.
- 12-week QBR delivered and signed off.
- Support entitlement and escalation contacts verified in PagerDuty and Zendesk.
- Knowledge transfer session recorded and uploaded.

Appendix: sample CLI & troubleshooting commands
- Validate connectivity (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Retrieve recent errors (example):
  rcli logs --tenant <TENANT_ID> --from "2027-02-27T00:00:00Z" --to "2027-02-28T00:00:00Z" --filter "status>=500"
